title: FlashAttention generations have distinct hardware and API contracts
summary: Select an attention generation using its actual GPU, dtype and interface requirements; package names and installation paths are not interchangeable.

hardware: FA2 CUDA: Ampere/Ada/Hopper; FA3: H100/H800; FA4 CuTeDSL targets Hopper/Blackwell in the inspected README
software: Dao-AILab/flash-attention at 1fc0221183e799363001394a12dd9e78e15f5dda; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Qualify exact head dimensions, masks, variable lengths and dtypes on the selected implementation

claims.description: FA3 documents FP16/BF16 forward/backward and FP8 forward, with CUDA >=12.3 and an H100/H800 requirement.
FA3 is installed from hopper and imported through flash_attn_3; FA4 uses flash-attn-4 and flash_attn.cute. The source keeps generation-specific installation and capability sections.

downstream_impact: vLLM and vLLM-Omni: audit optional imports and dispatch during dependency upgrades, especially where Hopper and Blackwell share a configuration.
vllm-ascend: use a separately qualified NPU implementation; this CUDA card supplies no compatible kernel.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Test supported and unsupported dtype/head-size/mask combinations against the same reference before benchmarking prefill or diffusion attention.
Measure kernel and full pipeline latency independently; include compilation/import cost and record the exact selected generation.
limitations: Different algorithms and FP8 can change numerical error; mathematical attention equivalence is not bitwise parity.
ROCm has separate implementation requirements in the source and is outside this CUDA card.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
